We also obtain a different rigidity result when the rotation number has positive exponential type: the boundary restriction of every $C^1$ pseudo-rotation is rigid and topologically conjugate to a rotation. We show that this boundary conclusion fails in the bi-Lipschitz class by constructing non-rigid examples for every rotation number of finite positive exponential type. The proof of rigidity is based on a finite-information closing theorem under H\"older regularity. For the construction of counterexamples, we use disjoint supports instead of a summable perturbation scheme.
item.dc:creator: Jian Wang, Peizheng Yu

item.title: Topological entropy and Burau representation
item.description: arXiv:math/0304105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let f be an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of the disk D, P a finite invariant subset and [f] the isotopy class of f in D\P. We give a non trivial lower bound of the topological entropy for maps in [f], using the spectral radius of some specializations in GL(n,C) of the Burau matrix associated with [f] and we discuss some examples.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Ser. I Math., 309(13) :835-838, 1989
item.dc:creator: Boris Kolev

item.title: The complete dynamics description of positively curved metrics in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$
item.description: arXiv:2307.06418v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The family of invariant Riemannian manifolds in the Wallach flag manifold $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$ is described by three parameters $(x,y,z)$ of positive real numbers. By restricting such a family of metrics in the \emph{tetrahedron} $\cal{T}:= x+y+z = 1$, in this paper, we describe all regions $\cal R \subset \cal T$ admitting metrics with curvature properties varying from positive sectional curvature to positive scalar curvature, including positive intermediate curvature notion's. We study the dynamics of such regions under the \emph{projected Ricci flow} in the plane $(x,y)$, concluding sign curvature maintenance and escaping. In addition, we obtain some results for positive intermediate Ricci curvature for a path of metrics on fiber bundles over $\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{T}^2$, further studying its evolution under the Ricci flow on the base.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo F. Cavenaghi, Lino Grama, Ricardo M. Martins, Douglas D. Novaes

item.title: Solvable Structures for Hamiltonian Systems
item.description: arXiv:2504.02189v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a geometric framework connecting solvable structures and integrable Hamiltonian systems. For a completely integrable Hamiltonian system with $n$ degrees of freedom, we construct a solvable structure consisting of $2n$ Hamiltonian vector fields that allows us to integrate Hamilton's equations by quadratures. Explicit expressions are derived for the associated Pfaffian forms whose integration yields both the solutions of Hamilton's equations and action-angle variables. This provides a novel interpretation of the Arnold-Liouville theorem in the context of solvable structures. We illustrate the theory by deriving explicit solutions and canonical variables of action-angle type for the open Toda lattice and the rational Calogero-Moser system.
item.dc:creator: Sasa Kresic-Juric, Concepcion Muriel, Adrian Ruiz

item.title: Infinite polynomial patterns in large subsets of the rational numbers
item.description: arXiv:2506.19667v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inspired by a question of Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson, we prove two new results about infinite polynomial configurations in large subsets of the rational numbers. First, given a finite coloring of $\mathbb{Q}$, we show that there exists an infinite set $B = \{b_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Q}$ such that $$\{b_i, b_i^2 + b_j : i < j\}$$ is monochromatic. Second, we prove that every subset of positive density in the rational numbers contains a translate of such an infinite configuration. The corresponding results in the integers are both known to be false, so our results provide natural and relatively simple examples of combinatorial structures that distinguish between the Ramsey-theoretic properties of the rational numbers and the integers. The proofs of our main results build upon methods developed in a series of papers by Kra, Moreira, Richter, and Robertson to translate from combinatorics into dynamics, where the core of the argument reduces to understanding the behavior of certain polynomial ergodic averages. The new dynamical tools required for this analysis are a Wiener--Wintner theorem for polynomially-twisted ergodic averages in $\mathbb{Q}$-systems and a structure theorem for Abramov $\mathbb{Q}$-systems.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Ackelsberg

item.title: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
item.description: arXiv:2509.08532v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $\beta$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $\beta$.
item.dc:creator: Carl P. Dettmann (University of Bristol, UK)

item.title: Deep Learning of Solver-Aware Turbulence Closures from Nudged LES Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2604.23874v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The differentiable physics paradigm may be leveraged as an a-posteriori approach for discovering turbulence closure models by embedding a neural network parameterization directly inside the solver and optimizing it given potentially sparse target data. This addresses a key limitation of a-priori learning where direct numerical simulation (DNS) data is used to approximate the subgrid stress with the assumption of a low-pass filter. Closures trained in this a-priori manner frequently lead to unstable deployments due to the mismatch between the assumed filter and the effect of numerical discretizations and coarse-graining. In comparison, while typically stable during deployment, a-posteriori learning incurs high computational costs due to the need to backpropagate through a large eddy simulation (LES) solver. Furthermore, a-posteriori methods are challenging to apply broadly since they require significant modification of existing solvers. Finally, both approaches are limited when generalization is desired across different numerical schemes with their implicit filtering characteristics. In this work, we present a deep-learning approach for turbulence closure modeling built on the continuous data assimilation framework. Our approach enables the a-priori training of closures using DNS data observed only at coarse-grid points without modifying or differentiating through the LES solver, while preserving stability during deployment for the recovery of long-term statistics. We focus on the model's ability to adapt to different discretizations by explicitly conditioning it on the numerical scheme. We use two- and three-dimensional canonical cases to test our framework and show that the learned correction systematically tracks the discretization error of the coarse solver.
item.dc:creator: Ashwin Suriyanarayanan, Dibyajyoti Chakraborty, Romit Maulik

item.title: Extracting Exact Lie Derivatives Without Backpropagation: A Dual Compiler for Neural Control Barrier Functions
item.description: arXiv:2604.23995v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A safety filter based on a neural control barrier function (CBF) evaluates, at each control cycle, the trained network and its Lie derivatives along the system vector fields. This paper presents a compiler whose emitted C++ code performs this evaluation on embedded processors by forward-mode differentiation with dual numbers. The derivatives are exact in the sense of automatic differentiation, which means that they are free of truncation error and subject to floating-point roundoff. One evaluation of the network in this arithmetic, called a dual pass, returns the barrier value and its Lie derivative along one vector field, and an extension to hyper-dual numbers returns the second-order Lie derivatives of CBFs of relative degree two. Apart from scalar variables, the memory that a dual pass writes is at most four floating-point numbers per neuron of the widest layer and does not depend on the network depth. On an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, we compare the emitted code with code for reverse-mode differentiation (i.e., backpropagation), which is also generated before the program runs and uses fixed-size arrays. In three experiments, the reverse-mode code has a lower execution time than the dual and hyper-dual passes executed one after the other. For single-input networks, the measurements do not establish such an ordering between the reverse-mode code and a variant of the dual pass that propagates the real part once. For networks of increasing depth, the working memory of the dual passes is constant, whereas that of the reverse-mode code increases. While the emitted code runs, no dynamic allocation is recorded. We report the maximum observed execution time of the complete filter step, which includes the dynamics and a breakpoint search for the quadratic program with input bounds and one affine constraint. The compiler and the experiments are open source.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Kamaldar

item.title: Learning Forced Multibody Dynamics on Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.12627v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce an architecture for learning the dynamics of forced mechanical systems evolving on Lie groups, based on discrete forced Euler-Lagrange equations. The proposed method, termed Lie Group Discrete Forced Euler-Lagrange Neural Network (LieDFLNN), learns mechanical dynamics directly from discrete configuration observations, without requiring velocity measurements. This formulation allows the simultaneous identification of unknown mechanical properties and forcing terms, while ensuring that the predicted configurations remain on the underlying Lie group. We develop explicit formulations for rigid body dynamics on $SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$, extend the framework to interacting multibody systems, and introduce a method for learning unknown control forces when the Lagrangian is known. Finally, we evaluate the method through numerical experiments involving rigid body dynamics, nonlinear external forces, controlled systems, and real-world human motion capture data. The numerical results confirm the advantages of incorporating Lie group geometry and discrete variational structure into data-driven modeling of forced mechanical systems.
item.dc:creator: Martine Dyring Hansen, Marta Ghirardelli, Elena Celledoni, David Martin de Diego, Brynjulf Owren

item.title: Differential inclusions and the chattering phenomenon
item.description: arXiv:2610.03561v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is a second draft of a manuscript about existence of solutions of differential inclusions involving chattering.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivanov

item.title: Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
item.description: arXiv:2611.09697v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2<1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions. We also show that the asymptotic variance for the Schwarzian derivative is at least $5.68\ldots$, which defeats the hypothesis that the Nehari criterion would be almost sharp.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: Averaging Principle and Uniform Large Deviations for Time-Dependent Slow-Fast Systems via Young-Rough Integration
item.description: arXiv:2611.16762v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The main aim of this work is to investigate the limiting behavior and asymptotic properties of time-dependent slow-fast stochastic dynamical systems. The slow component is driven by a stochastic process with H\"older-continuous paths of regularity greater than 1/2, while the fast component is driven by a Brownian rough path. We introduce a novel Young-rough integration framework tailored to such systems and establish well-posedness results, providing the analytical foundation for further asymptotic analysis. Building on this framework, we employ Khasminskii's time-discretization method to establish the strong convergence of the slow component to the solution of the corresponding averaged equation in the L^p-sense. Furthermore, when the driving noise in the slow equation is specified as a fractional Brownian motion, we apply the weak convergence approach to establish a uniform large deviation principle for the slow component, uniformly over compact sets of initial conditions, in the H\"older topology.
item.dc:creator: Wenting Xu

item.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for Hamilton--Jacobi equations with supercritical viscosity
item.description: arXiv:2611.20638v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $\sigma>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^\sigma\Delta u_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{\sigma-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.
item.dc:creator: Gengyu Liu, Zibo Wang, Jianlu Zhang

item.title: Power topologies and uniformities on bistochastic operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.26151v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the set of invertible Koopman operators attached to the usual interval probability space is dense (and hence dense $G_{\delta}$) in the space of bistochastic operators in the polynomial weak topology. This extends the non-polynomial analogue (due to Brown / Vershik / Ryzhikov / Eisner). We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results. Furthermore, the power topologies on the space of bistochastic operators recording weak convergence in powers up to $k+1$, $k\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ are all distinct, as are the analogous power uniformities on the automorphism group of the standard non-atomic Lebesgue probability measure.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu
